chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, saying: Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Nawanjiyy narrated to me, from Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Shu'ayri, from al-Rabi' — the companion of al-Mansur — who said:

Al-Mansur sent for al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, summoning him regarding something that had been reported to him about him. When he arrived at his gate, the chamberlain came out to him and said: 'I seek God's protection for you against the tyranny of this oppressor, for I have seen his rage against you is severe.' Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: 'I have from God a protecting shield that will aid me against him, if God wills. Seek permission for me to enter.' So he sought permission and it was granted. When he entered, he gave the greeting of peace, and al-Mansur returned it.

Then he said to him: 'O Ja'far, you well know that the Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him and his family, said to your father Ali ibn Abi Talib: "Were it not that factions of my community would say about you what the Christians said about Christ, I would say something about you such that you would pass no gathering without them taking the dust from beneath your feet to seek healing by it." And Ali, peace be upon him, said: "Two types of people will perish on my account, though I bear no guilt: the excessively devoted lover and the reckless defector." He said this as an apology from himself — that he does not approve of what the extremist or the defector says about him. By my life, if Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, had remained silent about what the Christians said of him, God would have tormented him. You know full well what false and slanderous things are said about you, and your silence about that and your contentment with it is the wrath of the Divine Judge.'

The riffraff of Hijaz and the rabble of the people claim that you are the scholar of the age and its supreme authority, the proof of the Worshipped One and His interpreter, the vessel of His knowledge and the scale of His justice — His lamp by which the seeker cuts through the breadth of darkness to the light of illumination; and that God does not accept any deed from any doer who is ignorant of your station in this world, nor raises for him on the Day of Resurrection any weight. So they have attributed to you beyond your proper rank and said about you what is not in you. Therefore speak! For the first to speak the truth was your grandfather, and the first to affirm it was your father, and you are well fitted to follow in their footsteps and tread their path.',

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: 'I am a branch from the branches of the olive tree, a lamp from the lamps of the House of Prophethood, the one disciplined by the angels, the ward of the noble and righteous, a lamp from the lamps of the niche that contains the Light of lights — the pure essence of the enduring Word, remaining in the lineage of the Chosen Ones until the Day of Gathering.'

Al-Mansur turned to those sitting with him and said: 'This man has referred me to a surging sea whose shore cannot be reached and whose depth cannot be fathomed — the scholars are bewildered in it and the swimmers drown in it, and the breadth of the open space becomes too narrow for the one swimming in it. He is the thorn lodged across the throats of the caliphs — one who cannot be exiled nor is it lawful to kill him. Were it not for the tree that unites him and me — a tree whose root is wholesome, whose branch has soared high, whose fruit is sweet, and which was blessed among atoms and sanctified in the ancient scriptures — I would have done to him what would not be praiseworthy in its consequences, because of what reaches me of his severe criticism of us and his ill speech about us.'

Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: 'Do not accept against your blood relative and those of your household who deserve care the word of one whom God has forbidden Paradise and made his abode the Fire; for the tale-bearer is a false witness and a partner of Iblis in sowing discord among people. Indeed God Almighty has said:',
O you who believe! If a dissolute person comes to you with a report, investigate, lest you afflict a people out of ignorance and then become regretful over what you have done. (Quran 49:6)

We are your supporters and helpers, and the pillars and foundations of your kingdom — so long as you command what is right and good, execute the rulings of the Quran among the subjects, and humiliate the nose of Satan through your obedience to God. And if it is incumbent upon you — given the breadth of your understanding, the abundance of your knowledge, and your acquaintance with the manners of God — to maintain ties with one who severs them from you, to give to one who deprives you, and to forgive one who wrongs you; for the one who merely reciprocates is not the one who truly maintains ties. The true upholder of ties is the one who, when his kinship bond is severed, rejoins it. So maintain your kinship ties, and God will extend your life and lighten your reckoning on the Day of your Gathering.',

Al-Mansur said: 'I have pardoned you in recognition of your standing and overlooked you on account of your truthfulness. So relate to me something about yourself by way of a hadith from which I may take admonition, something that will be for me a genuine deterrent against destructive acts.' Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: 'You must hold fast to forbearance, for it is the cornerstone of knowledge. Master yourself in situations when you have the power to act, for if you act as you are able, you will be like one who has satisfied a grudge, or treated a resentment, or who likes to be mentioned for his dominance. Know that if you punish one who deserves it, the greatest thing you can be described with is only justice; and I know no condition better than the condition of justice. But the condition that necessitates gratitude is better than the condition that necessitates patience.'

So the Prophet, may God's blessings be upon him and his family, gave him the glad tidings of that. Ali, peace be upon him, fell prostrate in gratitude to God, Exalted and Majestic. Then he raised his head and said: 'O Messenger of God, has my standing reached such a level that I am mentioned there?' He said: 'Yes, and indeed God knows you, and you are mentioned in the highest company.' Al-Mansur said: 'That is the bounty of God — He gives it to whom He wills.'

So the Prophet, may God's blessings be upon him and his family, gave him the glad tidings of that. Ali, peace be upon him, fell prostrate in gratitude to God, Exalted and Majestic. Then he raised his head and said: 'O Messenger of God, has my standing reached such a level that I am mentioned there?' He said: 'Yes, and indeed God knows you, and you are mentioned in the highest company.' Al-Mansur said: 'That is the bounty of God — He gives it to whom He wills.'

key_terms.الرَّفِيقُ الْأَعْلَى: The Highest Assembly — the exalted celestial realm mentioned in Quran
key_terms.الصادق: Al-Sadiq — epithet of Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad, the sixth Imam
key_terms.الْمِشْكَاةُ: The niche (from Quran 24:35) — metaphor for the source of divine light
key_terms.جُنَّةٌ وَاقِيَةٌ: A protective shield/armor — divine protection against harm
key_terms.حَبْرُ الدَّهْرِ: Sage of the age — the supreme religious authority of the time
key_terms.يَعْسُوبُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Chief/leader of the believers — a title of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say when summoned by the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts a tense meeting between Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur in 368 AH (as transmitted through the assembly of al-Saduq). Al-Mansur summoned the Imam allegedly to rebuke him for the extreme claims made by his followers, but al-Sadiq responded with eloquent self-description anchored in the light of prophethood. The exchange culminates in the Imam counseling al-Mansur on forbearance and governance, and sharing a exclusive hadith of the Night Journey in which God praised Imam Ali as the Imam of the God-fearing and Chief of the believers.
